**Minutes of Meeting Security Wearable Ecosystem**

**Date:** 21 July 2026, Singapore

**1\. Solution direction wearable, not app**

An app-only solution was ruled out. An app has no **defensible barrier** a competent developer can replicate it in weeks. A wearable device tied to a platform, corpus and control-room console creates a real barrier to entry.

**Locked:**

- Form factor: wrist-worn device (watch-style)
- GPS built in for location tracking and to detect when a device leaves the site rather than being handed over between shifts
- Cost target: SGD 20 to 30 per unit; hard ceiling SGD 100
- Camera: simple, not high-spec enough to record and interpret basic context
- Connectivity: cellular SIM only. WiFi is not workable sites do not have coverage. Confirmed by Siva's operational experience.
- Model: subscription-based, device recyclable across officers when they leave the agency

**2\. Data and connectivity**

- Voice payload is small (audio in KB, not GB), so data plans do not need to be heavy
- Dexter currently runs ~100 SIMs at SGD 8 per month (400GB) via SimTel for CIS cameras
- Dexter to negotiate volume pricing on the basis of 400+ SIMs - target below SGD 8, ideally SGD 5 to 6
- Package deal possible: **SIMs bundled through the new venture to end clients**

**3\. Go-to-market top-down, client-mandated**

Selling to security agencies alone will not work. Most agencies (bottom 75% of the market) cannot afford the device. The angle is to sell the assurance to the **end client** the property owner or manager and let the client mandate the device in their tender.

**Locked positioning:**

- Target the top 25% of security agencies who can absorb the cost
- Primary buyer: end clients (condos, commercial buildings, industrial sites)
- Pitch: "assurance that your SGD 6,000 security officer is actually earning it"
- Wedge: PWM salary rise from ~SGD 3,600 today to ~SGD 6,000 by 2028
- Public education channel (bus advertising, public campaigns) to build client awareness that this assurance exists

**4\. Software scope minimalist**

Full SOP dumps into the device were rejected. Different sites have different procedures, and the officer does not need 200 pages read back to him.

**Locked:**

- Emergency prompts limited to the 5-6 critical steps per scenario (fire, medical, break-in, etc.)
- Detailed SOPs remain in existing systems and on the officer's phone
- Incident report forms auto-generated in the format the regulator requires
- Deeper queries handled by the AI on demand if the officer asks - the system can go into the underlying document when needed
- Role-based access: supervisor sees site-level information only, not officer-to-device transcripts
- PDPA-compliant cloud (Singapore-hosted)
- Guardrails: security domain only. Personal calls, non-work queries and off-topic requests are blocked at the model layer. Precedent noted: past experience of site phones misused for international personal calls at agency cost.

**5\. Commercial structure new company**

**Locked:**

- Dexter and Siva to form a new Singapore Pte Ltd
- The new company is separate from current company
- The new company will supply the device and platform to CIS and to other agencies and clients
- Shareholding: Dexter and Siva
- Current Company acts as first design partner and early customer

**6\. Mahesh's role Technical expert**

**Locked:**

- Mahesh engages as **technical expert / service provider** on a retainer basis
- Project-level title: **Technical Director on the venture**
- Joint decision-making on device selection, with Dexter taking Mahesh's technical recommendation

**7\. Engagement path**

**Locked sequence:**

- NDA signed between Mahesh, Dexter and Siva as **individuals** (the new company does not yet exist)
- Retainer / service provider agreement executed once terms are agreed
- Once the new company is incorporated, engagement formalised at project level

**Dexter and Siva to draft the NDA**. Detail exchange on the Security-side operational intelligence (which is substantial and industry-specific) begins only after the NDA is signed.

**8\. IP path patent pending, India**

**Locked:**

- Engage a patent lawyer
- File patent application in India for patent-pending status
- Budget blocked: SGD 5,000
- Mahesh has prior experience previous filing cost ~SGD 3,000
- Full patent grant unlikely in the security space in India (industry incumbents have political weight), and that is accepted
- Patent pending is sufficient for the commercial purpose it signals commitment and uniqueness to investors and clients
- Do not attempt Singapore filing too expensive, and India filing generates the same questioning discipline for a fraction of the cost

**9\. Device sourcing India or Shenzhen**

**Locked:**

- Prototyping and manufacturing to happen in India or Shenzhen. Singapore is out cost base does not work.
- Supplier continuity requirement: minimum 3 to 4 years of production commitment. No fly-by-night manufacturers.
- Joint device decision Dexter to source and shortlist, Mahesh to recommend, Dexter takes recommendation

**10\. Timeline 3 to 4 month rollout target**

- Software build is not the bottleneck the platform can be assembled quickly
- The bottleneck is device prototyping and getting the unit economics right at scale
- Mahesh to produce a roadmap covering software, device, platform and commercial milestones
